Eight non-test files in `sklearn/` call `check_non_negative` directly. I checked this with the code index and with a plain grep, and both found the same call sites. It is never imported under a different name, and no module re-exports it, so every call uses the plain name.

- `sklearn/decomposition/_lda.py`: called in `LatentDirichletAllocation._check_non_neg_array`
- `sklearn/decomposition/_nmf.py`: called in `_check_init`, `_initialize_nmf`, `NMF._fit_transform` and `MiniBatchNMF._fit_transform`
- `sklearn/kernel_approximation.py`: called in `AdditiveChi2Sampler.fit` and `AdditiveChi2Sampler.transform`
- `sklearn/manifold/_t_sne.py`: called in `TSNE._fit`
- `sklearn/metrics/pairwise.py`: called in `pairwise_distances`
- `sklearn/naive_bayes.py`: called in `MultinomialNB._count`, `ComplementNB._count`, `CategoricalNB._check_X` and `CategoricalNB._check_X_y`
- `sklearn/neighbors/_base.py`: called twice in `_check_precomputed`
- `sklearn/utils/validation.py`: called in `_check_sample_weight`, in the same file where the function is defined
